_note: The Camera / Framing Lab's reproducible configurations. Cases 1-4 are the ten camera presets and the three canvases -- the interactions section 16 names -- on the fixture that already exists for them. Cases 5-8 are the line-of-sight work: 5 and 6 are the arm and the control of the production reproduction (a hero standing in front of another hero on glowmere-atmospherics), and 7 and 8 are the frustum's two aspect regimes. Every case names a fixture this repository already ships; none of them carries an expectation as a number, because a case that graded itself would be a probe grading itself.

cases.title: The camera-behaviour fixture, from the first shot
cases.question: Does each of the six shot-level camera behaviours do the thing the handbook says it does?
cases.expectation: Shot 1 the camera does not move, shot 2 it travels with the performer, shot 3 the performer stands still and the camera circles, shot 4 the camera is the performer. The differences are meant to be unarguable side by side in time, which is why this fixture is one clip rather than six.
cases.notes: The permanent visual fixture for the presets; it predates this lab and is registered rather than replaced. Render the whole thing with --render to see all six.

cases.title: The same second at the output's aspect ratio, portrait
cases.question: Is the preview's framing the deliverable's framing when the deliverable is not 16:9?
cases.expectation: The vertical field of view is identical to case 1 and the horizontal one is much narrower, because this engine fixes fovY and derives fovX from the aspect (ADR-246). Anything else means a canvas change is a reframe, which would make the Output Frame canvas a lie.
cases.notes: The arithmetic half is asserted in tests/unit/test_camera_lab_viewport.cpp; this is the case that lets a person look at it.

cases.title: The same second at an ultrawide aspect
cases.question: What does the terrain cull's 2.5 aspect floor cost, and where does it stop costing anything?
cases.expectation: Nothing visible changes -- that is the point. At 2.5:1 and wider the floor is inert, so this case is the control for case 4: it is the aspect at which the exact frustum and the floored one are the same frustum.
cases.notes: 2.5:1 exactly. Measured cost of the floor at narrower aspects, against a grid of chunk-sized boxes: +16.7% at 2.39:1, +33.3% at 16:9, +64.7% at 4:3, +100% at 1:1, +180% at 9:16.

cases.title: Terrain in portrait, where the cull frustum is four times the frame
cases.question: How much ground is submitted that the frame cannot contain?
cases.expectation: The picture is correct and the draw count is not. At 9:16 the terrain cull builds its frustum at 2.5 while the frame is 0.5625, so roughly 2.8x the ground survives the frustum test. Nothing is missing; the cost is entirely in what is kept.
cases.notes: The arm for case 3. Entity culling has no floor and uses the exact aspect, so the asymmetry is visible only in the terrain chunk counts.

cases.title: A hero standing in front of the hero the shot is framing
cases.question: Can the directed camera see the hero it is holding?
cases.expectation: On this project in continuous mode, four of the 185 baked keys that hold a hero were framing `spire-cap` from behind `elder-2-cap` before the sightline pass existed, and none are after it. The camera was correctly outside both heroes the whole time, which is why ADR-080's clearance never saw it.
cases.notes: Reproduced headlessly and measured in tests/unit/test_director_sightline.cpp, with a hand-written march against TerrainQuery::surfaceAt rather than against the query that does the fixing. Requires the Auto-director to be run on the project; the timeline as shipped is already baked.

cases.title: CONTROL for case 5: the same bake with the correction budget at zero
cases.question: Does the count in case 5 move because of the sightline pass, or would it have moved anyway?
cases.expectation: The four blocked keys are still blocked. AutoDirectorSettings::maxSightlineCorrection = 0 makes the pass a pure instrument -- it still finds every obstruction and still reports the correction it would have applied -- and the path comes back byte for byte.
cases.notes: ADR-182's control, and the reason case 5's number is a finding. Not reachable from the CLI: it is a settings value, and the arm that runs it is the test named above.

cases.title: The director's camera against the ground on the shipped Glowmere cut
cases.question: Does the clearance pass keep the baked camera out of the terrain and the canopy in production?
cases.expectation: It does, and by more than it needs to. 0 of 184 baked keys and 0 of 4001 interpolated samples sit below surface + 1.2 m. The uncleared bake's tightest sightline to its hero clears the ground by 0.63 m; after clearance it is 3.48 m -- so ADR-080's canopy lift is also doing most of the line-of-sight work against terrain, by accident.
cases.notes: Measured in tests/unit/test_director_terrain.cpp and tests/unit/test_director_sightline.cpp. The second is the reason this case is worth keeping: a count of zero that came from a margin of a few centimetres is a count the next terrain seed would not reproduce, and this one did not.

cases.title: A free-roaming viewport under a director that keeps cutting
cases.question: Does the viewport stay the artist's when the shot or the camera changes?
cases.expectation: It does, across a cut, a re-installed camera direction, an added camera and a resize in all three canvases -- and a following viewport still moves for all of them, which is what stops the first half being satisfied by a viewport that never moves at all.
cases.notes: Asserted headlessly in tests/unit/test_camera_lab_viewport.cpp. What this case will NOT show is protection from a seq::Shot's baked camera: a shot camera writes camera/position on the main camera, which is exactly the camera free-roam hands the viewport back to. See docs/camera-lab.md.
